Appendix: General considerations related to Crypto Assets1
As of the date of this report, crypto assets remain an evolving area of technology and marketplace
activity. Those who choose to invest in crypto assets should inform themselves of the general risks and
uncertainties associated with such assets.
(1) Crypto assets are owned anonymously. While the public keys of virtual wallets holding crypto assets
reside on the distributed networks and can be viewed publicly, the ownership of the wallets are
normally not registered and therefore, anonymous. Ownership of crypto assets is evidenced primarily by
the possession of the underlying private key (e.g. passcode). The possessor of the private key controls
the corresponding crypto asset wallet.
(2) Risk of irreversible transactions. Transactions for most crypto assets that occur over the blockchain
are generally irreversible, even if such transactions occur fraudulently or accidentally. If a private key is
lost or fraudulently used, the crypto assets in the corresponding wallet may not be recoverable.
(3) Regulatory uncertainty. Legislative and regulatory changes or actions at the state or federal level may
change or affect the use, transfer, exchange, and value of crypto assets. The effects of any such changes
are not determinable as of the date of this report.

Appendix: General considerations related to Crypto Assets1
As of the date of this report, crypto assets remain an evolving area of technology and marketplace
activity. Those who choose to invest in crypto assets should inform themselves of the general risks and
uncertainties associated with such assets.
(1) Crypto assets are owned anonymously. While the public keys of virtual wallets holding crypto assets
reside on the distributed networks and can be viewed publicly, the ownership of the wallets are
normally not registered and therefore, anonymous. Ownership of crypto assets is evidenced primarily by
the possession of the underlying private key (e.g. passcode). The possessor of the private key controls
the corresponding crypto asset wallet.
(2) Risk of irreversible transactions. Transactions for most crypto assets that occur over the blockchain
are generally irreversible, even if such transactions occur fraudulently or accidentally. If a private key is
lost or fraudulently used, the crypto assets in the corresponding wallet may not be recoverable.
(3) Regulatory uncertainty. Legislative and regulatory changes or actions at the state or federal level may
change or affect the use, transfer, exchange, and value of crypto assets. The effects of any such changes
are not determinable as of the date of this report.

agreement, where: a. the term of the agreement is overnight; and b. the counterparty to that

Ratings Services, or not less than Aa3 by Moody’s Investor Services”.

Appendix I: General considerations related to Crypto Assets1
As of the date of this report, crypto assets remain an evolving area of technology and marketplace activity.
Those who choose to invest in crypto assets should inform themselves of the general risks and
uncertainties associated with such assets.
(1) Crypto assets are owned anonymously. While the public keys of virtual wallets holding crypto assets
reside on the distributed networks and can be viewed publicly, the ownership of the wallets are normally
not registered and therefore, anonymous. Ownership of crypto assets is evidenced primarily by the
possession of the underlying private key (e.g. passcode). The possessor of the private key controls the
corresponding crypto asset wallet.
(2) Risk of irreversible transactions. Transactions for most crypto assets that occur over the blockchain are
generally irreversible, even if such transactions occur fraudulently or accidentally. If a private key is lost
or fraudulently used, the crypto assets in the corresponding wallet may not be recoverable.
(3) Regulatory uncertainty. Legislative and regulatory changes or actions at the state or federal level may
change or affect the use, transfer, exchange, and value of crypto assets. The effects of any such changes
are not determinable as of the date of this report.

To the Board of Directors of
Tether Holdings Limited
We have been engaged to perform a reasonable assurance engagement on the Consolidated Reserves
Report of Tether Holdings Limited (the “Company”) and its wholly owned subsidiaries Tether International
Limited (BVI), Tether Operations Limited (BVI), Tether Limited (Hong Kong), Alpha Group Commodities
Limited (BVI) and TG Commodities Limited (BVI) (the “Group”) as at 30 September 2023 (the “CRR”), a
copy of which has been attached to this report.
Management’s Responsibility for the CRR
Management is responsible for the preparation of the Consolidated Reserves Report in compliance with the
criteria, including Management’s Key Accounting Policies, set out in the CRR and for such internal control
as management determines is necessary to enable the preparation of CRR that is free from material
misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.
Auditors' Independence and quality control
We have complied with the independence and all other ethical requirements of the Code of Ethics for
Professional Accountants issued by the International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants, which is
founded on fundamental principles of integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care,
confidentiality and professional behaviour.
Our company applies International Standard on Quality Management 1, Quality Management for Firms
that Perform Audits or Reviews of Financial Statements, or Other Assurance or Related Services
Engagements (ISQM1) and, accordingly, maintains a system of quality control that includes directives and
procedures concerning compliance with ethical requirements, professional standards and applicable legal
and regulatory requirements.
Auditors’ responsibility
Our responsibility is to express our conclusion based on the procedures performed about the compliance of
the CRR with the criteria, including Management’s Key Accounting Policies, set out therein.
We carried out our work in accordance with the criteria established in the International Standard on
Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) ~ Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of
Historical Financial Information (“ISAE 3000 Revised"), issued by the International Auditing and Assurance
Standards Board (IAASB) for reasonable assurance engagements. This standard requires that we plan and
perform the engagement to obtain reasonable assurance whether the CRR is free from material
misstatement.
The procedures performed on the CRR are based on our professional judgement and include inquiries,
primarily of the company’s personnel responsible for the preparation of the information presented in the
CRR, analysis of documents, recalculations and other procedures aimed to obtain evidence, as
appropriate.
Specifically, we carried out the following procedures:
  obtain a comprehension of internal control system;

  verify, for a sample of outstanding secured loans, the existence of the collateral through the

  verify the correctness of the disclosures included in the CRR, excluding the Notes.
Conclusion
In our opinion, the CRR as prepared by the management of the Group as of 30 September 2023, is, in all
material respects, fairly presented in accordance with the criteria, including Management’s Key
Accounting Policies, set out therein.
Emphasis of Matter
We draw attention to the following in the accompanying CRR:
  The reporting date is limited to a point in time as of 30 September 2023. We did not perform
procedures or provide any assurance at any other date or time in this report.
  Management’s accounting policies provide the following:
-  financial investments are valued at fair value in line with IFRS 9;
-  investments in precious metals are valued at fair value;
-  intangible digital assets are valued at fair value;
-  secured loans are fully collateralized by liquid assets and constantly monitored and are measured
at amortised cost (notional value for short-term secured loans) and adjusted for any expected
credit loss allowance in line with IFRS 9;
-  tether tokens issued have been classified as refund liabilities in line with IFRS 9, which are
repayable on demand, and are recorded at the contractual redemption value of the tokens;
-  other assets and other liabilities are valued at amortised cost (notional value for short-term assets
and liabilities) less any expected credit losses.
  Management has applied a going concern basis of accounting to value the Group’s assets. The going
concern assessment requires significant management judgment with regards to the Group’s liquidity,
market and credit risks. We do not provide any assurance in respect of such assessment.
  The valuation of the assets of the Group have been based on normal trading conditions and does not
reflect unexpected and extraordinary market conditions, or the case of key custodians or
counterparties experiencing substantial illiquidity, which may result in delayed realisable values. No
provision for expected credit losses was identified by management at the reporting date.

  At the reporting date, Tether Holdings Limited and its wholly owned subsidiaries are defendant in

  The digital assets issued by the Group allow holders to transact and settle transactions in a rapid
manner, which may be pseudonymous, and may be verified by the sender and the recipient. The
digital asset industry is nascent and innovating rapidly. Accordingly, any users of digital assets,
including those tokens issued by the Group, should first inform themselves of the general risks and
uncertainties of the industry, including as to evolving legal and regulatory requirements. Users of
Tether tokens should familiarize themselves with the risk disclosures, as they may be changed and
updated from time to time.
Our opinion is not modified in respect of these matters.
Basis of Accounting
Without modifying our conclusion, we draw attention to the Management’s Key Accounting Policies
included in the CRR, which describe the basis of accounting. The CRR is prepared by management of
Tether Holdings Limited for transparency purposes. As a result, the CRR may not be suitable for another
purpose.
Scope limitations
Our opinion is limited solely to the CRR and the corresponding consolidated total assets and consolidated
total liabilities as of 30 September 2023. Activity prior to and after this time and date was not considered
when testing the balances and information described above. In addition, we have not performed any
procedures or provided any level of assurance on the financial or non-financial activity on dates or times
other than that noted within this report.
The Notes to the CRR are provided by management of the Group for additional information only, and this
information has not been subject to the scope of our assurance engagement and, accordingly, we do not
express an opinion or provide any assurance on it. Our responsibility is to read the other information in
the Notes, and, in doing so, consider whether the other information is materially inconsistent with the
CRR or our knowledge obtained in the course of the engagement, or otherwise appears to be materially

To the Board of Directors of
TETHER INTERNATIONAL, S.A. de C.V.
We have been engaged by Tether Global Investments Fund SICAF SA to perform a reasonable assurance
engagement on the Financials Figures and Reserves Report of Tether International, S.A. de C.V. (the
“Company”) as at 31 December 2025, a copy of which has been attached to this report.
Board of Director’s Responsibility for the Financials Figures and Reserves Report
The Board of Director is responsible for the preparation of the Financials Figures and Reserves Report in
compliance with the criteria, including Management’s Key Accounting Policies, set out in the Financials
Figures and Reserves Report and for such internal control as Board of Directors determines is necessary to
enable the preparation of the Financials Figures and Reserves Report that is free from material
misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.
Practitioner's Independence and quality control
We have complied with the independence and all other ethical requirements of the Code of Ethics for
Professional Accountants issued by the International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants, which is founded
on fundamental principles of integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality
and professional behaviour.
Our company applies International Standard on Quality Management 1, Quality Management for Firms that
Perform Audits or Reviews of Financial Statements, or Other Assurance or Related Services Engagements
(ISQM1) and, accordingly, maintains a system of quality control that includes directives and procedures
concerning compliance with ethical requirements, professional standards and applicable legal and regulatory
requirements.
Practitioner’s responsibility
Our responsibility is to express our conclusion based on the procedures performed about the compliance of
the Financials Figures and Reserves Report with the criteria, including Management’s Key Accounting Policies,
set out therein.
We carried out our work in accordance with the criteria established in the International Standard on
Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) ~ Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical
Financial Information (“ISAE 3000 Revised"), issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards
Board (IAASB) for reasonable assurance engagements. This standard requires that we plan and perform the
engagement to obtain reasonable assurance whether the Financials Figures and Reserves Report is free from
material misstatement.
The procedures performed on the Financials Figures and Reserves Report are based on our professional
judgement and include inquiries, primarily of the company’s personnel responsible for the preparation of the
information presented in the Financials Figures and Reserves Report, analysis of documents, recalculations
and other procedures aimed to obtain evidence, as appropriate.

Specifically, we carried out the following procedures:
▪  obtain an understanding of internal control over the preparation of the subject matter information
relevant to the engagement;
▪  perform enquiries with the management on the business operation of the last quarter, identifying
material changes;
▪  compare financial data between the current Financials Figures and Reserves Report and the ones of
the previous periods and discussion of possible significant differences;
▪  obtain confirmation letters directly from banks and depositaries and verify the reconciliations
performed by management between the amounts in the accounting ledger/system and the bank
statement to confirm the existence of the assets disclosed in the Financials Figures and Reserves
Report;
▪  obtain reports from a specialized provider relating to inventory and quality testing, on sample basis,
of precious metals and performing inventory procedures in order to confirm the existence of assets
disclosed in the Financials Figures and Reserves Report;
▪  verify, for a significant sample, the correct valuation of the assets disclosed in the Financials Figures
and Reserves Report in accordance with the criteria described in the Management’s Key accounting
policies;
▪  verify the reconciliations performed by management between the accounting ledger/system and the
ledgers on the various blockchains relating to assets and liabilities as at 31 December 2025;
▪  verify, for a sample of outstanding secured loans, the existence of the collateral through the analysis
of the contract and of the transactions;
▪  verify the correctness of the disclosures included in the Financials Figures and Reserves Report,
excluding the Notes.
Conclusion
In our opinion, the Financials Figures and Reserves Report, as prepared by the Board of Directors of the
Company as of 31 December 2025, is, in all material respects, fairly presented in accordance with the
criteria, including Management’s Key Accounting Policies, set out therein.
Emphasis of Matter
We draw attention to the following in the accompanying Financials Figures and Reserves Report:
▪  The reporting date is limited to a point in time as of 31 December 2025. We did not perform
procedures or provide any assurance at any other date or time in this report.
▪  Management’s Key Accounting Policies provide mainly the following:
- financial investments are valued at fair value in line with IFRS 9;
- investments in precious metals are valued at fair value;
- intangible digital assets are valued at fair value;
- secured loans are fully collateralized by liquid assets and regularly monitored and are measured at
amortised cost (notional value for short-term secured loans) and adjusted for any expected credit
loss allowance in line with IFRS 9;
- Tether tokens issued have been classified as refund liabilities in line with IFRS 9, which are
repayable on demand, and are recorded at the contractual redemption value of the tokens;
- other assets and other liabilities are valued at amortised cost (notional value for short-term assets
and liabilities) less any expected credit losses.
TETHER INTERNATIONAL, S.A. DE C.V. | Assurance Report according to ISAE 3000R  Page 2 of 3

[page 4]
▪  The Board of Directors has applied a going concern basis of accounting to value the Company’s assets.
The going concern assessment requires significant judgment with regards to the Company’s liquidity,
market and credit risks. We do not provide any assurance in respect of such assessment.
▪  The valuation of the assets of the Company is based on normal trading conditions and does not reflect
unexpected and extraordinary market conditions, or the case of key custodians or counterparties
experiencing substantial illiquidity, which may result in delayed realisable values. No provision for
expected credit losses was identified by management at the reporting date.
▪  At the reporting date, Tether International, S.A. de C.V. is defendant in two ongoing civil litigation
proceedings, for which the outcome cannot yet be reasonably and reliably estimated by the Board of
Directors and its counsels and therefore no provision is recognised by management.
▪  The digital tokens issued by Tether International, S.A. de C.V. allow holders to transact and settle
transactions in a rapid manner, which may be pseudonymous, and may be verified by the sender and
the recipient. The digital asset industry is nascent and innovating rapidly. Accordingly, any users of
digital assets, including those tokens issued by the Company, should first inform themselves of the
general risks and uncertainties of the industry, including as to evolving legal and regulatory
requirements. Users of Tether tokens should familiarize themselves with the risk disclosures, as they
may be changed and updated from time to time.
Our opinion is not modified in respect of these matters.
Basis of Accounting
Without modifying our conclusion, we draw attention to the Management’s Key Accounting Policies included
in the Financials Figures and Reserves Report, which describe the basis of accounting. The Financials Figures
and Reserves Report is prepared by the Board of Directors of Tether International, S.A. de C.V. for
transparency purposes. As a result, the Financials Figures and Reserves Report may not be suitable for
another purpose.
Scope limitations
Our opinion is limited solely to the Financials Figures and Reserves Report and the corresponding total assets
and total liabilities as of 31 December 2025. Activity prior to and after this time and date was not considered
when testing the balances and information described above. In addition, we have not performed any
procedures or provided any level of assurance on the financial or non-financial activity on dates or times
other than that noted within this report.
The Notes to the Financials Figures and Reserves Report are provided by the Board of Directors of the
Company for additional information only, and this information has not been subject to the scope of our
assurance engagement and, accordingly, we do not express an opinion or provide any assurance on it. Our
responsibility is to read the other information in the Notes, and, in doing so, consider whether the other
information is materially inconsistent with the Financials Figures and Reserves Report or our knowledge
obtained in the course of the engagement, or otherwise appears to be materially misstated.

to its customers. We, as members of management, are responsible for complying with the requirements of the New
York State Department of Financial Services (“DFS”) industry letter dated June 8, 2022, Guidance on the Issuance
of U.S. Dollar-Backed Stablecoins (the “DFS Letter”). We are also responsible for establishing and maintaining
effective internal controls over compliance with the requirements of the DFS Letter. We have performed an
evaluation that includes all relevant matters of the Company’s compliance with item 1(a), paragraph 2, and
item 3(a) of the DFS Letter during the period from May 1, 2026 to May 31, 2026.
In accordance with item 3(a) of the DFS Letter, we assert that the Company has complied with the following
requirements as of the dates noted below (“Management’s Assertion”):
•  The amounts disclosed below for GUSD issued and in circulation and the Reserve (as defined below) as
of May 4, 2026 and as of May 29, 2026, at end of day are accurate;
•  The Reserve was, at these times, adequate to fully back all outstanding GUSD issued and in circulation;
and
•  All DFS-imposed conditions on the Reserve assets (whether set forth in paragraph 2 of the DFS Letter or
otherwise specified by DFS) have been met.
The Company is required to comply with the following provisions of the DFS Letter:
•  Item 1(a) under the DFS Letter requires that a U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin must be fully backed by asset
reserves (the “Reserve”), meaning that the market value of the Reserve is at least equal to the nominal
value of all outstanding units of the stablecoin as of the end of each business day. Per the DFS Letter, “end
of day” is implied to be 5pm Eastern Time. As a practical matter our reconciliation process begins within
30 minutes of 5pm Eastern Time and takes a number of minutes to complete the necessary transfers which
could mean that the reconciliation process is completed shortly after 5pm Eastern Time.
Paragraph 2 of the DFS Letter includes the following provisions:
o  Item 2(a) under the DFS Letter requires that assets in the Reserve must be segregated from the
proprietary assets of the issuing entity, and must be held in custody with (i) U.S. state or federally
chartered depository institutions with deposits insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
(“FDIC”) and/or (ii) asset custodians, approved in advance in writing by DFS. The Reserve assets
shall be held at these depository institutions and custodians for the benefit of the holders of the
stablecoin, with appropriate titling of accounts.
o  Item 2(b) under the DFS Letter describes the types of permissible assets the Reserve may hold,
including deposit accounts at state or federally chartered depository institutions, government
money market funds, U.S. Treasury bills with maturities of three months or less, and certain reverse
repurchase agreements fully collateralized on an overnight basis. DFS imposes additional
restrictions and provisions with regard to these asset types, which are described in Item 2(b).
o  Item 2(c) under the DFS Letter explains the Company is expected to manage the liquidity risk of
the Reserve in accordance with the redemption requirements discussed in paragraph 1 of the DFS
Letter.

Paxos Digital Singapore Pte. Ltd. (the "Company") was granted a Major Payment Institution (MPI) license by
the Monetary Authority of Singapore (“MAS”) to issue stablecoins on 1 July 2024.
The Global Dollar token (“USDG”) is a cryptographic token, which allows financial market participants to
transact in a crypto asset that has been pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar by the Company. The Company maintains
the redemption assets securing USDG in approved asset categories per the requirements set by MAS. USDG
is deployed on the Ethereum network and is an ERC-20 token, which is built on the Ethereum public blockchain.
As such, the number of USDG tokens in circulation is fully and transparently viewable at all times by anyone
through any publicly available Ethereum block explorer (e.g. Etherscan).
2. DISCUSSIONS RELATED TO CRYPTO ASSETS
As of the date of this report, crypto assets remain an evolving area of technology and marketplace activity.
Those who choose to invest in crypto assets should inform themselves of the general risks and uncertainties
associated with such assets.
a. Ownership of Crypto assets:
Crypto assets are owned anonymously. While the public keys of virtual wallets holding crypto assets reside
on the distributed networks and can be viewed publicly, the ownership of the wallets is normally not
registered and therefore, anonymous. Ownership of crypto assets is evidenced primarily by the possession
of the underlying private key (e.g. passcode). The possessor of the private key controls the corresponding
crypto asset wallet.
b. Risk of irreversible transactions:
Transactions for most crypto assets that occur over the blockchain are generally irreversible, even if such
transactions occur fraudulently or accidentally. If a private key is lost or fraudulently used, the crypto assets
in the corresponding wallet may not be recoverable.
c. Regulatory uncertainty:
Legislative and regulatory changes or actions may change or affect the use, transfer, exchange, and value
of crypto assets. The effects of any such changes are not determinable as of the date of this report.

1. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDED BY PAXOS TRUST COMPANY, LLC
Paxos Trust Company, LLC (the “Company”) is a New York limited purpose trust company. The Company
received its trust charter from the New York Department of Financial Services in 2015 and has been a long-
time leader in both crypto asset services and the creation of blockchain technologies for the financial world.
The Pax Dollar token (“USDP”) is a cryptographic token, which allows financial market participants to
transact in a crypto asset that has been strictly pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar by the Company. The Company
maintains the redemption assets securing USDP in segregated accounts that are unencumbered and held
on behalf of USDP holders in one or more of the following forms: (i) fiat currency held in FDIC-insured bank
accounts; (ii) (a) investments (including through overcollateralized overnight reverse repurchase
agreements) in debt instruments that are expressly guaranteed by the full faith and credit of the United
States Government; and/or (b) money-market funds composed of such debt instruments. Amounts backed
by debt instruments that are expressly guaranteed by the full faith and credit of the United States
Government are subject to market pricing risk. Fiat deposits held at insured depository institutions may be
in excess of FDIC insurance limits. USDP is deployed on the Ethereum network and the Solana network
and is an ERC-20 token, which is built on the Ethereum public blockchain, and an SPL token, which is built
on the Solana public blockchain. As such, the number of USDP tokens in circulation is fully and
transparently viewable at all times by anyone through any publicly available Ethereum block explorer and
Solana block explorer (e.g. Etherscan and Solscan).
2.  DISCUSSIONS RELATED TO CRYPTO ASSETS GENERALLY
As of the date of this report, crypto assets remain an evolving area of technology and market place activity.
Those who choose to invest in crypto assets should inform themselves of the general risks and uncertainties
associated with such assets.
(1) Crypto assets are owned anonymously. While the public keys of virtual wallets holding crypto assets
reside on the distributed networks and can be viewed publicly, the ownership of the wallets are normally
not registered and therefore, anonymous. Ownership of crypto assets is evidenced primarily by the
possession of the underlying private key (e.g. passcode). The possessor of the private key controls the
corresponding crypto asset wallet.
(2) Risk of irreversible transactions. Transactions for most crypto assets that occur over the blockchain are
generally irreversible, even if such transactions occur fraudulently or accidentally. If a private key is lost or
fraudulently used, the crypto assets in the corresponding wallet may not be recoverable.
(3) Regulatory uncertainty. Legislative and regulatory changes or actions at the state or federal level may
change or affect the use, transfer, exchange, and value of crypto assets. The effects of any such changes
are not determinable as of the date of this report.

1. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDED BY PAXOS DIGITAL SINGAPORE PTE LTD
Paxos Digital Singapore Pte. Ltd. (the "Company") was granted a Major Payment Institution (MPI) license by
the Monetary Authority of Singapore (“MAS”) to issue stablecoins on 1 July 2024.
The Global Dollar token (“USDG”) is a cryptographic token, which allows financial market participants to
transact in a crypto asset that has been pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar by the Company. The Company maintains
the redemption assets securing USDG in approved asset categories per the requirements set by MAS. USDG
is deployed on the Ethereum network, the Solana network, and the Ink network. It exists as an ERC-20 token
on the Ethereum public blockchain and Ink Blockchain and an SPL token on the Solana blockchain. As such,
the number of USDG tokens in circulation is fully and transparently viewable at all times by anyone through
any publicly available Ethereum block explorer, Solana block explorer, and Ink block explorer (e.g. Etherscan,
Solscan, and Ink Explorer).
2. DISCUSSIONS RELATED TO CRYPTO ASSETS
As of the date of this report, crypto assets remain an evolving area of technology and marketplace activity.
Those who choose to invest in crypto assets should inform themselves of the general risks and uncertainties
associated with such assets.
a. Ownership of Crypto assets:
Crypto assets are owned anonymously. While the public keys of virtual wallets holding crypto assets reside
on the distributed networks and can be viewed publicly, the ownership of the wallets is normally not
registered and therefore, anonymous. Ownership of crypto assets is evidenced primarily by the possession
of the underlying private key (e.g. passcode). The possessor of the private key controls the corresponding
crypto asset wallet.
b. Risk of irreversible transactions:
Transactions for most crypto assets that occur over the blockchain are generally irreversible, even if such
transactions occur fraudulently or accidentally. If a private key is lost or fraudulently used, the crypto assets
in the corresponding wallet may not be recoverable.
c. Regulatory uncertainty:
Legislative and regulatory changes or actions may change or affect the use, transfer, exchange, and value
of crypto assets. The effects of any such changes are not determinable as of the date of this report.

MANAGEMENT’S ASSERTION
Standard Custody & Trust Company, LLC (the “Company”), a subsidiary of Ripple Labs Inc. as the ultimate
parent company, is a New York limited purpose trust company and the issuer of Ripple USD (“RLUSD”), a U.S.
dollar-denominated stablecoin. The Company is responsible for the completeness, accuracy, and validity of the
RLUSD Reserve Report as of February 19, 2026, and February 27, 2026, at 5:00pm Eastern Time (the “Report
Dates”). The Company’s Management asserts that as of the Report Dates:
●  The Market Value of the Assets in the Reserve, both in aggregate and broken down by asset class, and
the quantity of Outstanding Stablecoin Units in the RLUSD Reserve Report are presented in accordance
with the criteria below,
●  The Market Value of the Assets in the Reserve was equal or greater than the Outstanding Stablecoin
Units, and
●  The DFS-imposed Conditions on the Assets in the Reserve have been met.
CRITERIA
This criteria was derived from items 3(a)(i) through 3 (a)(iv) set forth in Paragraph 3 of the industry letter issued
by the New York State Department of Financial Services (“DFS”) dated June 8, 2022, Guidance on the Issuance
of U.S. Dollar-Backed Stablecoins (the “NYDFS Letter”).
1. Market Value means the total balance of U.S. dollar denominated Assets in the Reserve at the Report
Dates held by the Company with regulated financial institutions on behalf of RLUSD holders.
2. Reserve means the account utilized by Management to hold the Assets on behalf of RLUSD holders at
the Report Dates. The Reserve is segregated from the proprietary assets of the Company.
3. Outstanding Stablecoin Units means the aggregate amount of RLUSD currently present on the XRP
Ledger and Ethereum blockchain networks at the Report Dates.
4. DFS-imposed Conditions means:
o  The Assets in the Reserve must be segregated from the proprietary assets of the issuing entity,
and must be held in custody with (i) U.S. state or federally chartered depository institutions with
deposits insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”) and/or (ii) asset
custodians, approved in advance in writing by the DFS.
o  The Assets in the Reserve consist of the following classes:
▪ U.S. Treasury bills acquired by the Issuer three months or less from their respective
maturities.
▪ Reverse repurchase agreements fully collateralized by U.S. Treasury bills, U.S.
Treasury notes, and/or U.S. Treasury bonds on an overnight basis, subject to DFS-
approved requirements concerning overcollateralization. Such reverse repurchase
agreements shall be either (A) tri-party or (B) bilateral with a counterparty whose identity
has been submitted to DFS in writing, without objection, at least 14 days prior to the
Issuer’s commencing to enter into contracts with such counterparty.
▪ Government money-market funds, subject to DFS-approved caps on the fraction of the
Reserve assets to be held in such funds and DFS-approved restrictions on the funds,
such as a minimum percentage allocation to direct obligations of the Government of the
United States and reverse repurchase agreements on such obligations.
▪ Deposit accounts at US State or federally chartered depository institutions, subject to

Notes to the Redemption Assets Report
February 5, 2024 and February 29, 2024 at 5:00pm ET
(No Assurance Provided by the Independent Accountant on These Notes)
1. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDED BY PAXOS TRUST COMPANY, LLC
Paxos Trust Company, LLC (the “Company”) is a New York limited purpose trust company. The Company
received its trust charter from the New York Department of Financial Services in 2015 and has been a long-
time leader in both crypto asset services and the creation of blockchain technologies for the financial world.
The Pax Dollar token (“USDP”) is a cryptographic token, which allows financial market participants to
transact in a crypto asset that has been strictly pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar by the Company. The Company
maintains the redemption assets securing USDP in segregated accounts that are unencumbered and held
on behalf of USDP holders in one or more of the following forms: (i) fiat currency held in FDIC-insured bank
accounts; (ii) (a) investments (including through overcollateralized overnight reverse repurchase
agreements) in debt instruments that are expressly guaranteed by the full faith and credit of the United
States Government; and/or (b) money-market funds composed of such debt instruments. Amounts backed
by debt instruments that are expressly guaranteed by the full faith and credit of the United States
Government are subject to market pricing risk. Fiat deposits held at insured depository institutions may be
in excess of FDIC insurance limits. USDP is deployed on the Ethereum network and the Solana network
and is an ERC-20 token, which is built on the Ethereum public blockchain, and an SPL token, which is built
on the Solana public blockchain. As such, the number of USDP tokens in circulation is fully and
transparently viewable at all times by anyone through any publicly available Ethereum block explorer and
Solana block explorer (e.g. Etherscan and Solscan).
2.  DISCUSSIONS RELATED TO CRYPTO ASSETS GENERALLY
As of the date of this report, crypto assets remain an evolving area of technology and market place activity.
Those who choose to invest in crypto assets should inform themselves of the general risks and uncertainties
associated with such assets.
(1) Crypto assets are owned anonymously. While the public keys of virtual wallets holding crypto assets
reside on the distributed networks and can be viewed publicly, the ownership of the wallets are normally
not registered and therefore, anonymous. Ownership of crypto assets is evidenced primarily by the
possession of the underlying private key (e.g. passcode). The possessor of the private key controls the
corresponding crypto asset wallet.
(2) Risk of irreversible transactions. Transactions for most crypto assets that occur over the blockchain are
generally irreversible, even if such transactions occur fraudulently or accidentally. If a private key is lost or
fraudulently used, the crypto assets in the corresponding wallet may not be recoverable.
(3) Regulatory uncertainty. Legislative and regulatory changes or actions at the state or federal level may
change or affect the use, transfer, exchange, and value of crypto assets. The effects of any such changes
are not determinable as of the date of this report.

experiencing substantial illiquidity, which may result in delayed realisable values. No provision for
expected credit losses was identified by management at the reporting date.
▪  At the reporting date, Tether International, S.A. de C.V. is defendant in two ongoing civil litigation
proceedings, for which the outcome cannot yet be reasonably and reliably estimated by the Board of
Directors and its counsels and therefore no provision is recognised by management.
▪  The digital tokens issued by Tether International, S.A. de C.V. allow holders to transact and settle
transactions in a rapid manner, which may be pseudonymous, and may be verified by the sender and
the recipient. The digital asset industry is nascent and innovating rapidly. Accordingly, any users of

general risks and uncertainties of the industry, including as to evolving legal and regulatory
requirements. Users of Tether tokens should familiarize themselves with the risk disclosures, as they

Criteria

of assets (in any combination): i. cash; ii. cash equivalent; iii. bonds or notes with no more than
three months residual maturity, that is issued by either: a. the government or public entity of the
country that the currency of the SCS is pegged to; or b. a recognised multilateral agency; or iv.
any bonds or notes stated in sub-paragraph b. iii. above that are held under a reverse repurchase
agreement, where: a. the term of the agreement is overnight; and b. the counterparty to that
agreement holds a long-term rating of not less than AA- by Fitch Ratings or Standard and Poor’s
Ratings Services, or not less than Aa3 by Moody’s Investor Services”.

Background1
Paxos Digital Singapore Pte. Ltd. and Paxos Issuance Europe Oy (together “Paxos”, or the “Company”) are
issuers of Global Dollar (“USDG”). Paxos Digital Singapore Pte. Ltd. (PDS) was granted a Major Payment

and redeem e-money tokens on 23 November 2022 and is regulated by the Finnish Financial Supervisory
Authority (“FIN-FSA”).
The Global Dollar token (“USDG”) is a cryptographic token that allows financial market participants to
transact in a crypto asset pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar. USDG is issued and redeemed by PDS and PIE
under a multi-jurisdictional compliance model in consideration of MAS’s upcoming stablecoin regulatory
framework and compliant with MiCA’s e-money token requirements, including capital, segregation of
reserves, redemption at par, and ongoing disclosures.

Redemption Assets Report as of April 8, 2026 and April 30, 2026 at 5:00 pm United States Eastern Time

Appendix I: General considerations related to Crypto Assets1
As of the date of this report, crypto assets remain an evolving area of technology and marketplace activity.
Those who choose to invest in crypto assets should inform themselves of the general risks and
uncertainties associated with such assets.
(1) Crypto assets are owned anonymously. While the public keys of virtual wallets holding crypto assets
reside on the distributed networks and can be viewed publicly, the ownership of the wallets are normally
not registered and therefore, anonymous. Ownership of crypto assets is evidenced primarily by the
possession of the underlying private key (e.g. passcode). The possessor of the private key controls the
corresponding crypto asset wallet.
(2) Risk of irreversible transactions. Transactions for most crypto assets that occur over the blockchain are
generally irreversible, even if such transactions occur fraudulently or accidentally. If a private key is lost
or fraudulently used, the crypto assets in the corresponding wallet may not be recoverable.
(3) Regulatory uncertainty. Legislative and regulatory changes or actions at the state or federal level may
change or affect the use, transfer, exchange, and value of crypto assets. The effects of any such changes
are not determinable as of the date of this report.

합의된 절차 수행결과 보고서
디지털엑스 주식회사 귀중  2026 년 8 월 19 일
우리는 별도 첨부한 디지털엑스 주식회사(이하 “회사”)의 요청에 따라 2026 년 7 월 31 일 기준 회사가
운영 중인 가상자산거래소 업무와 관련하여 보유한 가상자산 수량의 확인, 가상자산 지갑 통제권 및
소유권과 관련하여 아래와 같이 회사와 합의한 절차를 수행하였습니다.
본 업무는 한국공인회계사회가 제정한 합의된 절차 수행업무기준에 따라 수행되었습니다. 본 보고서는
'특정 금융거래정보의 보고 및 이용에 관한 법률' 제 8 조 (가상자산 사업자의 조치)와 동법 시행령 제 10
조의 18(실명확인입출금계정의 개시)에 따라, 데이터베이스 상의 가상자산 수량을 실제로 보유하고 있는
지에 대한 확인과 회사가 보유하고 있는 가상자산 지갑 통제권 및 소유권의 실재성에 대한 확인을
목적으로 합니다. 우리가 수행한 절차는 회사가 금융기관에 제출하는 자료를 작성하는데 도움이 되고자
수행한 것이며, 본 보고서는 이 목적 이외에 다른 목적으로는 사용되어서는 아니됩니다. 회사와의
합의에 따라 우리가 수행한 절차를 요약하면 다음과 같습니다.
1. 우리는 회사가 제공한 2026 년 7 월 31 일 24 시 기준 BTC 외 19 종의 가상자산 수량과 내부 데이터
베이스에서 관리되는 수량이 일치하는지 여부에 대하여 실사 업무를 수행하였습니다.
2. 우리는 회사가 제공한 지갑 명세 중 중요도 및 위험도를 고려하여 표본 추출된 지갑에 대해
소액이전테스트(Penny Transfer Test)를 실시하여 가상자산의 전송 및 통제 절차가 적절히 수행되는지
여부에 대하여 실사 업무를 수행하였습니다.
업무수행결과는 우리의 발견사항은 다음과 같습니다.
“항목 1” 관련: 회사 소유의 전자지갑을 확인하여 2026 년 7 월 31 일 현재 데이터베이스 상 고객이
예치한 보유수량 대비 100.29%의 가상자산이 보관된 것을 확인하였습니다.
“항목 2” 관련: 소액이전테스트를 직접 실시하고 관련 절차를 직접 관찰한 결과, 회사의 내부 보안
규정에 따른 전송 수행과 통제 절차가 준수되고 있음을 확인하였습니다.
별첨 보고서는 상기 합의된 절차를 적용하여 산출된 보고서입니다. 합의된 절차에 따른 실사의 결과,
회사는 '특정 금융거래정보의 보고 및 이용에 관한 법률' 제 8 조(가상자산사업자의 조치)와 동법 시행령
제 10 조의 18(실명확인입출금계정의 개시)에 따라, 회사의 데이터베이스에서 관리되는 수량은 회사가
제시한 가상자산의 보유수량과 일치하며 회사 보유의 가상자산 지갑 통제권 및 소유권이 실재하고
있습니다. 상기 절차는 회계감사기준에 따른 감사나 재무제표 등에 대한 검토업무기준을 적용한
검토업무가 아니므로 우리는 2026 년 7 월 31 일 현재 고객별 거래내역 분리관리절차와 가상자산 지갑
통제권 및 소유권에 대하여 어떠한 확신도 표명하지 않습니다. 또한, 회계기록 유지 및 재무제표 산출에
대한 책임은 회사의 경영자에게 있으며, 우리의 업무는 경영자의 승인을 받지 아니한 계정, 거래 또는

[page 3]
회계기록에 대한 회계처리의 결정, 변경 또는 재분류 및 거래의 결제 또는 승인과 같은 경영의사결정을
포함하고 있지 아니합니다.
따라서, 우리가 회사와 합의한 절차 외에 추가적인 절차를 수행하거나 회계감사기준에 따른 감사나
검토업무기준에 따른 검토업무를 수행하였다면 회사에 보고할 다른 문제가 발견될 수도 있습니다.
본 보고서는 첫번째 문단에서 언급된 목적 및 회사의 정보 제공용도로만 이용되어야 되는 것이며
제 3 자에게 배포되거나 다른 목적으로는 사용될 수 없습니다. 또한, 본 보고서는 상기에서 언급한 특정
항목에만 관련된 것이며, 회사의 전체 재무제표로 확대될 수 없습니다.
회  계  법  인  해  솔
대  표  이  사  김 성 용

[page 4]
II. 가상자산 보유수량 실사
1) 가상자산 보유수량 실사의 개요
실 사 기 관: 회계법인 해솔
실 사 업 무: 가상자산 보유수량 테스트를 위하여 회사보유 전자지갑에 대한
http://etherscan.io 등 외부조회 사이트 조회 및 외부보관 가상자산(Bitgo,
Fireblocks 에 보관)에 대해 전자지갑을 제공한 업체의 웹사이트에서 조회
실 사 기 간: 2026. 8. 13 ~ 2026. 8. 18
실 사 장 소: 디지털엑스㈜ 본사(서울시 강남구 테헤란로 5 길 7, 4 층) 및 회계법인 해솔
2) 가상자산 보유수량 실사의 진행 절차
회사의 전자지갑을 조회할 수 있는 외부 사이트(Blockchain Explorer)의 주소와 회사의
전자지갑의 Public key 를 확보하여 직접보관 중인 가상자산을 조회 확인하고, Bitgo, Fireblocks
에 외부보관 중인 전자지갑에 대하여는 전자지갑을 제공한 업체의 웹사이트에서 조회하여 해당
자산이 실재하고 있음을 확인했습니다. 또한 이용자 위탁 가상자산의 종목 및 지갑 수 등을
고려하여 당 법인이 판단한 합리적인 범위내에서 당 법인이 지정하는 다른 공개주소로 소량의
가상자산을 이전하도록 요청하고, 해당 요청대로 가상자산이 이전되었는지를 블록체인에서
확인하는 테스트를 통해 가상자산 지갑소유권 및 개인키 통제여부를 확인하였습니다.
3) 가상자산 보유수량 실사의 결과
회사에서 제시한 가상자산은 총 20 종이며, 회사가 보유한 전자지갑에 보관되어 있습니다.
실사 결과, 실사기준일 현재 회사가 보유한 전자지갑에는 고객이 예치한 보유수량 대비 100.29%의
가상자산이 보관되어 있는 것으로 확인되었으며, 그 실사 결과는 다음과 같습니다. 당 법인은
회사가 제시한 가상자산에 대해 외부사이트 조회 등의 방법으로 실사한 수량과 회사의 내부
데이터베이스에서 관리되는 수량이 일치하는지 대사 하였으며, 회사가 제시하지 않은 가상자산에
대해서는 그 실재성과 완전성 등을 보장하지 않습니다.

[page 6]
III. 지갑 소유권 확인 실사
1) 지갑 소유권 확인 실사의 개요
실 사 기관: 회계법인 해솔
실 사 업무: 가상자산 지갑 소유권 확인 실사
실 사 기간: 2026.07.24
실 사 장소: 디지털엑스㈜ 본사(서울시 강남구 테헤란로 5 길 7, 4 층)
2) 지갑 소유권 확인 실사의 의의 및 목적
회사가 보유하고 있다고 주장하는 가상자산 지갑의 통제권 및 소유권이 회사에 실재함을
확인하기 위하여, 감사인이 지정한 외부 지갑주소로 가상자산을 전송하여 가상자산 지갑 보유
및 통제에 대한 독립적 증거를 확보하기 위함입니다.
3) 지갑 소유권 확인 실사의 진행 절차
본 가상자산 지갑 소유권 확인 실사의 진행 절차는 회사가 제시한 지갑 명세 중, 중요도 및
위험도를 고려하여 표본 추출된 지갑에 대해 감사인이 지정한 외부 지갑주소로 가상자산을
실제 전송하는 소액이전테스트(Penny Transfer Test)를 직접 실시하고, 전송 및 통제 절차를
직접 관찰(Observation)하는 방법으로 수행하였습니다.
4) 지갑 소유권 확인 실사의 제한
본 지갑 소유권 확인 실사는 회사 제공자료에 대한 이해를 바탕으로 합리적인 수준의 실사로
제한된 자료 및 시간에 수행되었으며 실사 기준일을 고려하여 현재시점의 현황과 다를 수
있습니다.
5) 지갑 소유권 확인 실사의 결과
실사 결과, 실사기준일 현재 회사는 내부 보안 규정에 따라 전송 수행과 통제 절차가 준수되고
있음을 확인하였으며, 그 실사 결과는 다음과 같습니다. 당 법인이 제시한 수취 지갑 주소로
사전에 합의된 소액을 전송 직후 블록체인 네트워크상에서 해당 트랜잭션이 생성되고
승인되는 과정을 모니터링하여 회사보유 가상자산 지갑의 통제권 및 소유권 확인하였으며,
회사가 제시하지 않은 가상자산 지갑에 대한 통제권과 소유권 등을 보장하지 않습니다.

합의된 절차 수행결과 보고서
두나무 주식회사 귀중
서울특별시 서초구 강남대로 369
우리의 보고서(이하 “보고서”)는 두나무 주식회사(이하 “회사”)가 운영 중인 https://www.upbit.com (이하 “업비트”)의
디지털자산거래소 업무와 관련하여, 회사가 보유한 실사 대상 디지털자산에 대하여 대한민국 표준시(KST) 2026년 8월 31일
24시(2026년 9월 1일 00시, 이하 “실사기준일”) 기준으로 실사를 수행하고 그 결과를 보고하기 위한 목적으로만
작성되었습니다. 본 합의된 절차에서 디지털자산은 경제적 가치를 지닌 것으로서 전자적으로 거래 또는 이전될 수 있는 전자적
증표를 뜻하며, 실사 대상 디지털자산은 BTC, ETH, XRP, ETC, DOGE, XLM, CRO, ATOM, LINK, DOT, SAND, AXS,
STX, NEAR, SOL, ENS, CTC, AVAX, SHIB, APT, ARB, ONDO, PEPE, ENA, WLD 총 25종입니다.
우리는 2026년 3월 15일자 계약 및 2026년 7월 24일자 부속합의서를 통해 회사와 합의된 절차를 아래와 같이
수행하였으며, 발견사항은 다음과 같습니다.
절차 1: 우리는 실사기준일 현재 회사가 보유한 실사 대상 디지털자산의 수량 및 원화환산금액을 업비트 이용자(이하
“이용자”)가 위탁한 실사 대상 디지털자산의 수량 및 원화환산금액과 비교하였습니다. 디지털자산의 수량을 원화
금액으로 환산 시 적용한 원화환산가치는 업비트의 실사기준일 현재 거래가격을 사용하였습니다. 절차 수행 결과,
회사가 보유한 실사 대상 디지털자산의 수량 및 원화환산금액은 이용자의 디지털자산의 수량 및 원화환산금액을
초과하고 있음을 확인하였습니다.
절차 2: 우리는 실사기준일 현재 회사가 이용자 위탁자산을 보관하기 위해 개설 및 운영하는 지갑 내에 보유한 실사
대상 디지털자산별 수량(이하 “이용자 위탁 분산원장 수량”)을 이용자가 위탁한 실사 대상 디지털자산별 수량(이하
“이용자 위탁 전산원장 수량”)과 비교하였습니다. 절차 수행 결과, 실사 대상 디지털자산별 이용자 위탁 분산원장 수량은
이용자 위탁 전산원장 수량을 초과하고 있음을 확인하였습니다.
절차 3: 우리는 실사기준일 현재 회사가 보유한 실사 대상 디지털자산별 수량을 블록체인 데이터 수량조회 결과 및 기타
회사가 제시한 증빙과 대사하였습니다. 절차 수행 결과, 회사가 보유한 실사 대상 디지털자산의 수량은 블록체인
데이터에서 조회한 수량 및 기타 회사가 제시한 증빙 상 수량과 일치하였음을 확인하였습니다.
2

[page 3]
절차 4: 우리는 실사기준일 현재 회사가 소유 및 통제하고 있는 실사 대상 디지털자산 지갑 중 임의의 지갑을 선정하여
회사가 보유하는 다른 지갑으로 우리가 제시한 소량의 디지털자산을 이전하도록 요청하고, 해당 요청대로 디지털자산이
이전되었는지 확인하는 절차(이하 “소액 이전 테스트”)를 수행하였습니다. 절차 수행 결과, 블록체인 데이터를 통해
회사가 우리의 요청대로 디지털자산을 이전하였음을 확인하였습니다.
절차 5: 우리는 실사기준일 현재 회사가 소유 및 통제하고 있는 실사 대상 디지털자산 지갑 중 임의의 지갑을 선정하여
우리가 제시한 원본 메시지를 암호학적 알고리즘에 따라 회사가 전자서명 하도록 요청하고, 해당 전자서명이 유효한지
검증하는 절차(이하 “전자서명 검증”)를 수행하였습니다. 절차 수행 결과, 회사가 제공한 전자서명은 유효한 서명임을
확인하였습니다.
절차 6: 우리는 실사기준일 현재 이용자의 실사 대상 디지털자산별 수량을, 2026년 7월 31일 기준 이용자의
디지털자산별 수량에 회사가 제시한 2026년 8월 1일부터 2026년 8월 31일까지 이용자의 디지털자산별 거래내역 및
입출금수량을 가감하여 산출한 이용자 위탁수량 계산결과와 대사하였습니다. 절차 수행 결과, 실사기준일에 이용자의
실사 대상 디지털자산별 수량은 이용자 위탁수량 계산결과와 일치하였음을 확인하였습니다.
절차 7: 우리는 실사기준일 현재 이용자의 실사 대상 디지털자산별 수량을 회사가 제시한 이용자 명부 등 여타 자료 상
디지털자산별 수량과 대사하였습니다. 절차 수행 결과, 이용자의 실사 대상 디지털자산별 수량은 이용자 명부 등 여타
자료 상 디지털자산별 수량과 일치하였음을 확인하였습니다.
절차 8: 우리는 절차 1 ~ 절차 7 수행내역 및 결과를 포함하여 회사의 디지털자산 실사보고서를 작성하였습니다.
우리는 한국공인회계사회가 제정한 합의된 절차 수행업무 기준(2006)에 따라 본 합의된 절차 업무를 수행하였습니다. 합의된
절차 업무는 우리가 회사와 합의한 절차를 수행하고, 합의된 절차 수행 결과 발견된 사실을 보고하는 업무입니다. 우리는 위에
설명된 합의된 절차가 본 보고서를 요청받은 목적 또는 다른 목적을 위해 적절한지에 대한 어떠한 진술도 하지 않으며,
디지털자산의 출처와 관련 신빙성을 확인할 의무는 없습니다.
우리는 IESBA의 국제윤리기준 및 한국공인회계사회의 공인회계사윤리기준을 준수하였습니다. 이 업무의 목적을 위하여
우리는 공인회계사의 독립성 요구사항을 준수할 의무가 없습니다.
상기 절차는 회계감사기준에 따른 감사나 재무제표 등에 대한 검토업무기준을 적용한 검토업무가 아니므로, 우리는
실사기준일 현재 회사의 디지털자산에 대하여 어떠한 확신도 표명하지 않습니다. 따라서 우리가 회사와 합의한 절차 외에
3

[page 4]
추가적인 절차를 수행하거나 회계감사기준에 따른 감사나 검토업무기준에 따른 검토업무를 수행하였다면 회사에 보고할 다른
문제가 발견될 수도 있습니다.
본 보고서는 첫번째 문단에서 언급된 목적 및 회사의 정보 제공용도로만 이용되어야 하며, 다른 목적으로 사용되거나 배포될
수 없습니다. 또한 본 보고서는 상기에 언급한 특정계정과 항목에만 관련된 것이며, 회사의 전체 재무제표로 확대될 수
없습니다.

[page 5]
1. 실사용역 개요
1.1 용역의 일반사항
(1) 용역 기간: 2026년 8월 31일 ~ 2026년 9월 14일
(2) 실사 장소: 두나무 본사 및 전산실
(3) 실사기준일: 대한민국 표준시(KST) 2026년 8월 31일 24시 (2026년 9월 1일 00시)
1.2 디지털자산 실사 방법
당 법인은 실사기준일에 회사를 직접 방문하여 회사가 관리하는 실사 대상 디지털자산에 대한 실사를 진행하였습니다.
회사는 업비트에서 거래되는 실사 대상 디지털자산에 대해 회사가 생성한 내부 전자지갑에 보관하고 있으며,
업비트에서 스테이킹 서비스를 지원하는 실사 대상 디지털자산에 대해서는 별도의 스테이킹 주소에 보관하고
있습니다.
(1) 내부 전자지갑
회사가 제시한 실사 대상 디지털자산별 수량을 블록체인 조회를 통해 확인한 수량과 비교하였습니다. 온체인 정보
확인을 위해 당 법인은 블록체인 익스플로러 사이트의 정보를 조회했고, 회사는 개별 Node 의 분산원장 및 블록체인
익스플로러 사이트 등의 정보를 조회했습니다.
(2) 스테이킹 주소
회사가 제시한 실사 대상 디지털자산별 스테이킹 수량을 블록체인 조회를 통해 확인한 수량과 비교하였습니다. 온체인
정보 확인을 위해 회사는 개별 Node 의 분산원장 및 블록체인 익스플로러 사이트 등의 정보를 조회했습니다.
5

2. 실사 결과
2.1 실사 결과 요약
디지털자산 실사 결과, 실사기준일 현재 회사가 보유한 실사 대상 디지털자산 수량 및 원화환산금액은 이용자의 실사
대상 디지털자산 수량 및 원화환산금액을 초과하고 있습니다. 보유비율은 원화환산금액 기준으로 약 103.64%입니다.
디지털자산별 원화환산가치는 업비트의 실사기준일 현재 거래가격을 사용하였습니다. BTC 마켓에서만 거래 가능한
디지털자산의 경우 해당 디지털자산의 가격을 KRW 마켓 상의 BTC 가격으로 환산하였으며, USDT 마켓에서만 거래
가능한 디지털자산의 경우 해당 디지털자산의 가격을 KRW 마켓 상의 USDT 가격으로 환산하였습니다.

주식회사 코인원 귀중
우리는 별도 첨부한 주식회사 코인원의 2026년 08월 31일 현재의 가상자산 수량과 관련
하여 아래와 같이 회사와 합의한 절차를 수행하였습니다. 본 업무는 한국공인회계사회가
제정한 합의된 절차 수행업무기준에 따라 수행되었습니다. 우리가 수행한 절차는 가상자
산이 회사의 고유재산과 회원의 재산으로 구분되어 관리되고 있음을 확인하는 회사의 내
부통제에 도움이 되고자 수행된 것이며 본 보고서는 귀하의 정보목적으로만 이용되어야
합니다. 귀하와의 합의에 따라 우리가 수행한 절차를 요약하면 다음과 같습니다.
1. 가상자산 수량 실재성 및 과부족 검증
용역 기준일 현재 회사가 보유하고 있는 가상자산 수량에 대하여 지갑주소별 외부조
회 시스템 및 스냅샷 등을 대조하여 실재성을 확인하였으며, 회사와 협의하여 실사
대상으로 선정한 가상자산의 수량을 확인하기 위하여 거래소 서버와 연결되어 있는
Hot Wallet과 거래소 서버에 연결되지 않고 별도의 저장장치에 보관되어 있는 Cold
Wallet에 보관된 해당 가상자산의 수량을 전수 조사하였습니다.
회사가 보유하고 있는 가상자산 수량과 회사의 데이터베이스상 회원의 가상자산 수
량을 대사하여 데이터베이스상 회원의 가상자산 수량 대비 회사가 보유하고 있는 가
상자산 수량의 과부족 여부를 확인하였습니다.
2. 가상자산 지갑 통제권 검증
용역 기준일 현재 회사가 보유하고 있는 가상자산 지갑 중 일부를 선정하여 지정한
주소로 소액을 실제 이전하여 해당 지갑의 통제권을 확인하였습니다.
-  2 -

[page 3]
업무수행결과는 다음과 같습니다.
항목 1관련: 용역 기준일 현재 실사 대상으로 선정한 가상자산의 실재성을 확인하였으
며, 회사가 보유한 가상자산 수량은 데이터베이스상 회원이 소유한 가상자
산을 초과하고 있습니다(회원이 예치한 가상자산 대비 원화 환산 기준
100.09% 보유). 위 확인은 실사 대상으로 선정한 가상자산에 한정합니다.
항목 2관련: 용역 기준일 현재 회사가 해당 지갑의 자산을 이전할 수 있음을 검증하여
회사 보유 가상자산 지갑의 통제권을 확인하였습니다. 위 확인은 회사가 제
시한 지갑 및 가상자산에 한정하며, 회사가 제시하지 않은 지갑이나 가상자
산의 통제권은 보장하지 아니합니다.
상기 절차는 회계감사기준에 따른 감사나 재무제표 등에 대한 검토업무기준을 적용한 검
토업무가 아니므로 우리는 2026년 08월 31일 현재의 주식회사 코인원의 별첨명세서에 대
하여 어떠한 확신도 표명하지 않습니다.
따라서, 우리가 주식회사 코인원과 합의한 절차 외에 추가적인 절차를 수행하거나 회계
감사기준에 따른 감사나 검토업무기준에 따른 검토업무를 수행하였다면 주식회사 코인원
에 보고할 다른 문제가 발견될 수도 있습니다.
본 보고서는 첫번째 문단에서 언급된 목적 및 주식회사 코인원의 정보 제공용도로만 이
용되어야 하며 제3자에게 배포되거나 다른 목적으로는 사용될 수 없습니다. 또한 본 보
고서는 상기에서 언급한 특정계정과 항목에만 관련된 것이며 주식회사 코인원의 전체 재
무제표로 확대될 수 없습니다.
[별첨] 가상자산 상세내역
-  3 -

[page 4]
서울시 강남구 남부순환로 2913(대치동, 동하빌딩 6층)
-  4 -

[page 5]
[별첨] 가상자산 상세내역
회사가 이용자로부터 위탁을 받아 보관하고 있는 가상자산은 2026년 08월 31일 기준 총
562종이며, 이 중 회사와 협의하여 거래지원 중인 가상자산 가운데 20종을 실사 대상으
로 선정하였습니다. 선정한 가상자산은 이용자 위탁 가상자산 가치의 95.85%에 해당합니
다. 원화 금액은 코인원 마켓에서 거래 가능한 가상자산의 경우, 용역기준일 시점 현재
코인원 마켓 내 최종 체결가를 적용하였으며, 코인원에서 거래되지 아니하는 가상자산의
경우 용역기준일 시점의 코인마켓캡(https://coinmarketcap.com)의 가격을 준용하여 산
정하였습니다.
실사 대상 가상자산은 회사가 보유한 가상자산 지갑 또는 관계 법령으로 정하는 기준에
따라 회사가 위탁 보관하고 있는 가상자산 지갑에 보관되어 있습니다. 용역기준일 현재
회사가 보유한 가상자산 지갑 등에는 회원계좌의 가상자산 수량보다 많은 수량이 보관되
어 있는 것으로 확인되었습니다. 회사가 보관하고 있는 실사대상 가상자산의 내역은 다

USDC Reserve Report
Management’s Assertion
Circle Internet Financial, LLC (“Circle” or the “Company”) is responsible for the completeness, accuracy and validity of the
USDC Reserve Report (“the Report”) as of June 10, 2024 and June 28, 2024 at 11:59pm Paciﬁc Daylight Time (the “Report
Dates”). Circle management asserts that the Fair Value of Assets Held in USDC Reserve is equal to or greater than USDC in
Circulation at the Report Dates in accordance with the criteria deﬁned in the Report below.
USDC Reserve Report
Report Dates  June 10, 2024  June 28, 2024
USDC in Circulation  32,006,867,453  32,222,674,248
(as deﬁned in the criteria below)
Fair Value of Assets Held in USDC Reserve  $  32,058,317,792  $  32,274,321,543
(as deﬁned in the criteria below)
CRITERIA
A. USDC In Circulation is deﬁned as the total USDC supply on USDC Approved Blockchains at the Report Dates
(32,952,831,646 and 33,450,832,753, respectively) less (i) Tokens Allowed But Not Issued as reported on USDC
Approved Blockchains (866,008,186 and 1,148,202,498, respectively) and (ii) Access Denied Tokens as reported on
USDC Approved Blockchains (79,956,007 and 79,956,007, respectively).
USDC Approved Blockchains are comprised of the Algorand, Arbitrum One, Avalanche C-Chain, Base, Celo, Ethereum,
Flow, Hedera, NEAR, Noble, OP Mainnet, Polkadot Asset Hub, Polygon PoS, Solana, Stellar, TRON, and ZKsync Era
blockchains and are used by the Company to issue and redeem USDC (with the exception of TRON for which only
redemptions are supported).
Tokens Allowed But Not Issued are deﬁned as tokens that exist on the Algorand, Hedera, Polkadot Asset Hub, and
Solana blockchains and are not currently issued to a USDC Holder. They are required due to the technical
implementation of USDC on those blockchains.
Access Denied Tokens are deﬁned as the amount of USDC tokens that are restricted from being accessed by the
holder to comply with a law, regulation, or legal order from a duly recognized U.S. authorized authority, U.S. court of
competent jurisdiction, or other governmental authority with jurisdiction over the Company.
B. Fair Value of Assets Held in USDC Reserve is deﬁned as the total balance of U.S. dollar denominated assets at the
Report Dates in the Circle Reserve Fund and in Segregated Accounts held by the Company with regulated ﬁnancial
institutions on behalf of USDC holders.
The Circle Reserve Fund (the “Fund”) is a government money market fund under Rule 2a-7 of the Investment Company
Act of 1940, as amended. The Company owns one hundred percent of the equity interests in the Fund represented by
the Fund’s Net Asset Value (the “NAV”), held on behalf of USDC holders. The Reserve Report provides details of the
fair value of the underlying net assets of the Fund that make up the NAV.
Segregated Accounts are unencumbered accounts held on behalf of USDC holders that are segregated from other
accounts of the Company, including general corporate funds.

GUSD RESERVES REPORT
Gemini Trust Company, LLC (the “Company”) has issued Gemini dollars (“GUSD”), a U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin,
to its customers. We, as members of management, are responsible for complying with the requirements of the New
York State Department of Financial Services (“DFS”) industry letter dated June 8, 2022, Guidance on the Issuance
of U.S. Dollar-Backed Stablecoins (the “DFS Letter”). We are also responsible for establishing and maintaining
effective internal controls over compliance with the requirements of the DFS Letter. We have performed an
evaluation that includes all relevant matters of the Company’s compliance with item 1(a), paragraph 2, and item
3(a) of the DFS Letter during the period from November 1, 2023 to November 30, 2023.
In accordance with item 3(a) of the DFS Letter, we assert that the Company has complied with the following
requirements as of the dates noted below (“Management’s Assertion”):
  The amounts disclosed below for GUSD issued and in circulation and the Reserve (as defined below) as
of November 15, 2023 at end of day and November 30, 2023 at end of day are accurate;
  The Reserve was, at these times, adequate to fully back all outstanding GUSD issued and in circulation;
and
  All DFS-imposed conditions on the Reserve assets (whether set forth in paragraph 2 of the DFS Letter or
otherwise specified by DFS) have been met.
The Company is required to comply with the following provisions of the DFS Letter:
  Item 1(a) under the DFS Letter requires that a U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin must be fully backed by asset
reserves (the “Reserve”), meaning that the market value of the Reserve is at least equal to the nominal
value of all outstanding units of the stablecoin as of the end of each business day. Per the DFS Letter, “end
of day” is implied to be 5 pm Eastern Time. As a practical matter our reconciliation process begins within
30 minutes of 5 pm Eastern Time and takes a number of minutes to complete the necessary transfers which
could mean that the reconciliation process is completed shortly after 5 pm Eastern Time.
Paragraph 2 of the DFS Letter includes the following provisions:
o  Item 2(a) under the DFS Letter requires that assets in the Reserve must be segregated from the
proprietary assets of the issuing entity, and must be held in custody with (i) U.S. state or federally
chartered depository institutions with deposits insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
(“FDIC”) and/or (ii) asset custodians, approved in advance in writing by DFS. The Reserve assets
shall be held at these depository institutions and custodians for the benefit of the holders of the
stablecoin, with appropriate titling of accounts.
o  Item 2(b) under the DFS Letter describes the types of permissible assets the Reserve may hold,
including deposit accounts at state or federally chartered depository institutions, government money-
market funds, U.S. Treasury bills with maturities of three months or less, and certain reverse
repurchase agreements fully collateralized on an overnight basis. DFS imposes additional
restrictions and provisions with regard to these asset types, which are described in Item 2(b).
o  Item 2(c) under the DFS Letter explains the Company is expected to manage the liquidity risk of the
Reserve in accordance with the redemption requirements discussed in paragraph 1 of the DFS
Letter.

Standard Custody & Trust Company, LLC (the “Company”), a subsidiary of Ripple Labs Inc. as the ultimate

method: 문항 86개 전부: 원문 sha256 재계산, jev_choice_test.pdf_pages로 입력 글을 다시 만들어 text, input_pages와 글자 단위 대조, 지운 줄이 원 쪽 글에 한 번씩 있었는지 확인(어긋남 0건).

레포 보고서 문항: data/reports*.json 값과 tests/test_rule_inputs.py 단계표(CIRC, CUST), R08은 tests/test_paxos.py, test_gemini.py, test_ripple.py, test_tether.py가 확인하는 attestation.type과 정답(만든 문항은 original_gold, 미정 문항은 repo_value) 대조(어긋남 0건).
근거 글: 예 정답은 입력 글에서 서명자 이름과 직함, 기관 이름, 정의나 계산 문장을 직접 찾았다. 아니오 정답은 기관 이름 꼴과 은행, 수탁사, 운용사 이름 60여 개, 계산 말(burn, mint, frozen, less, exclud 등), 경영진 확인 말(assert, approved, undersigned 등)로 남은 글 전체를 찾았다.
그림 쪽: Anchorpoint 2건, 코인원 4쪽(대주회계법인 대표이사 김영백, 도장), 코빗 5쪽(수량 표)을 그림으로 열어 서명 주체를 확인했다.
레포 밖 원문 3개(코빗, 업비트, 코인원) 사본의 sha256이 원래 위치 파일(Desktop, scratchpad/verify/F-1/web)과 같다.

question.ko: 이 글은 발행사가 보유자에게 이자(보유 기간에 비례한 금전 이익)를 주지 않는다고 밝히는가
question.instructions_suggested: Does this text state that holders do not receive interest, yield, or other returns from the stablecoin issuer for holding the stablecoin?

criteria_suggested.true: The text says holders are not entitled to, or will not earn, interest or returns from holding the issuer's token or from the assets backing it, or that the token does not generate, or is not designed to create, returns for holders.
criteria_suggested.false: The text has no such statement. A sentence that only says who keeps the income earned on reserve assets, or that describes rewards paid by a distributor or exchange, does not count.

question.note: 질문 문구는 제안이다. 아니오 쪽 설명에 함정 종류를 다 적지 않았다(적으면 문구 찾기가 된다).

terms.gold_rule: 예: 보유자나 토큰을 주어로, 보유자가 이자, 수익(returns), 금전 이익을 받지 않는다(not entitled, will not earn, does not generate)거나 토큰이 보유자에게 수익을 만들도록 설계되지 않았다(not designed to create returns)는 문장이 글 안에 있다. 아니오: 그런 문장이 없다. 다음만 있는 글은 아니오다: 발행사가 준비금 수익을 가진다는 문장(발행사가 주어), 보유자에게 준비자산 소유권이 없다는 문장, 유통사나 거래소가 주는 보상, 예금이 아니다 같은 상품 성격 고지, 수수료를 받지 않는다는 문장, 다른 뜻의 interest(security interest, ownership interest, right, title and interest, equity interest, conflicts of interest).

source_check.refetch_curl: 2026-10-09 22:26에 공식 주소 9건을 curl로 다시 받아 뽑은 글이 저장본과 줄 단위로 모두 같다(Paxos 2건, Ripple은 HTML 바이트까지 같다). Coinbase는 403(Cloudflare 확인 화면)이다.
source_check.coinbase_aside: Aside 브라우저로 다시 열어 innerText와 대조했다. 저장본 본문 줄이 모두 들어 있고, 빠진 154줄은 메뉴, 언어 목록, 쿠키 창 글이다. 개정일 Last updated: July 22, 2026 같음. USDC Rewards 절(493~501행)은 이어 붙인 글까지 같다.
source_check.webfetch: 개정일과 문항 근거 문장을 대조했다. Circle USDC(2025-12-12, 284행과 292행 문장), Circle EEA(2026-07-07, 3.3, 8.5, 9.5 전문, 발행사 Circle France), Circle EURC(2025-12-12), Paxos 약관(2026-06-30, 1.1.1, 3.1.8, 3.2.3의 interest 문장), USDG 백서(2026-06-24, A.14와 E.6 첫 문장, 보유자 이자 부정 문장 없음), Ripple(2024-10-03, 2.1(a)와 2.1(c) 전문, 발행사 SCTC), Tether(2026-02-26, About Tether Tokens 첫 두 문장, returns와 yield 없음), Gemini(2026-08-21, Your Fiat Currency의 interest 문장, Gemini Dollar 절에 interest 없음, Rewards 첫 문장). PayPal은 WebFetch가 73자 껍데기만 받아 curl 대조로 갈음했다. Coinbase는 WebFetch도 403이다.
source_check.note: fetch_terms.py는 첫 <title> 태그를 문서 제목으로 잡는다. 오늘 다시 받은 Gemini HTML은 svg 아이콘 title이 먼저 나와, 다시 돌리면 머리 줄 문서 제목이 Icon/Instagram이 된다. 본문 글에는 영향이 없다.

excluded.T17: 같은 글 안에 유통사 PayPal이 보유 잔액에 연율로 매일 쌓아 주는 보상(PYUSD Rewards, 94~108행)이 있고, 83행은 발행사 Paxos가 "당신의 PYUSD 몫" 준비금 이자를 PayPal과 나눌 수 있다고 적는다. 질문이 정의한 이자(보유 기간에 비례한 금전 이익)에 이 보상이 그대로 맞는다. 발행사가 직접 주는 것만 세면 예, 유통사를 거쳐 가는 것도 세면 아니오라 R14 판단 기준을 먼저 정해야 한다. 보상 절이 없는 같은 문장은 T30(예)으로 남는다.
excluded.T22: 정답 아니오가 gold_rule과 어긋난다. 490행 "you will not receive any portion of such compensation"은 보유자가 주어인 금전 이익 부정 문장이라 gold_rule의 예 조건에 맞는다. 또 이자가 생기면 같은 금액을 수수료로 Gemini가 가져간다는 문장(결과로 보유자 이자 0)과 이자가 붙지 않는 계좌라는 문장이 함께 있다. 절이 거래소 법정화폐 잔액과 GUSD 준비금 계좌를 섞어 다뤄 "보유자"가 누구인지도 갈린다.

1. About USDC
USDC is a digital token issued by Circle Internet Financial, LLC (“Circle”) that operates on each of the blockchains listed here (collectively, as of any date of determination, the “USDC Supported Blockchains”, and each such digital token, “USDC”). USDC issued by Circle is regulated as a form of stored value or prepaid access under the laws governing money transmission (or the statutory equivalent) in the various U.S. states and territories. For the avoidance of doubt, these Terms only apply to USDC held by persons located outside of the EEA.
From July 1st 2024, Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS will become a second, or “dual issuer” of USDC. See USDC White Paper for more information.
USDC is fully backed by an equivalent amount of U.S. Dollar-denominated assets held by Circle with U.S. regulated financial institutions in segregated accounts apart from Circle’s corporate funds, on behalf of, and for the benefit of, Users (the “Segregated Accounts”). This means that for every USDC issued by Circle and remaining in circulation, Circle will hold on behalf of Users either one U.S. Dollar (“USD”) or an equivalent amount of USD-denominated assets in its Segregated Accounts (the “USDC Reserves”). USDC is not designed to intrinsically create returns for holders, increase in value, or otherwise accrue financial benefit to the USDC holder.

items.clause:
3. Your Circle Mint Account
3.1. Your Circle Mint Account is an electronic money account which enables you to hold Circle Coins, which are e-money tokens. Further details on Circle Coins can be found in these Terms of Use at Section 9 (About Circle Coins).
3.2. Your Circle Mint Account is funded with Circle Coins and this represents the only available denomination at this time.
3.3. Subject to Section 8 (Closing your Circle Mint Account) below, the Circle Coins held in your Circle Mint Account do not expire but will not earn any interest.
3.4. You have the right to submit a request to redeem Circle Coins from your Circle Mint Account at any time, subject to the conditions set out in these Terms of Use, the applicable White Paper, the applicable Redemption Policy, and applicable law. Holders of EURC have a right of redemption at any time and at par value, in accordance with applicable law and MiCAR. Holders of USDC have a right of redemption at any time and at par value where they are located in the European Economic Area (“EEA”), in accordance with applicable law and MiCAR. For holders of USDC located outside the EEA, please refer to the specific USDC terms of Circle Internet Financial, LLC, and not to these Terms. For the avoidance of doubt, any reference to “at any time” refers to the ability to submit a redemption request and does not guarantee immediate or uninterrupted execution. Execution of redemption requests is subject to applicable law, regulatory requirements, compliance processes, and Circle France’s internal risk management frameworks, including but not limited to compliance, prudential, liquidity, and operational considerations. You may be required to confirm your identity before any redemption request is processed. Circle France may apply verification procedures, controls, delays, or limitations to redemption requests in accordance with Section 10.2 (Redemption of Circle Coins) of these Terms of Use. There is no minimum redemption amount but the Circle Coins in your Circle Mint Account must be sufficient to cover any applicable amounts owed to Circle France. Nothing in this section shall limit Circle France’s rights set forth in Section 13.1 (Insufficient Funds).
3.5. Electronic money accounts are not bank accounts. By accepting these Terms of Use you acknowledge that the French Deposit Guarantee Scheme (FDGS) does not apply to your Circle Mint Account. In the unlikely event that we become insolvent, you may lose the electronic money held in your Circle Mint Account. However, the European Electronic Money Directive 2009/110/EC, Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation4 ("MiCAR") and French national legislation apply to us and these laws are designed to ensure the safety and liquidity of funds deposited in electronic money accounts even in insolvency situations. For further information on how we safeguard our customers’ Circle Coins balance, please visit this Website page.
3.6. The electronic money in a Circle Mint Account belongs to the entity which is registered as the Circle Mint Account holder. No person other than the Circle Mint Account holder has any rights in relation to the Account Balance held in a Circle Mint Account.
3.7. By registering for a Circle Mint Account on behalf of an entity, you represent and warrant that:
3.7.1. such legal entity is duly organised and validly existing under the applicable laws of the jurisdiction of its organisation;
3.7.2. you are duly authorised by such legal entity to act on its behalf; and
3.7.3. such organisation (and any affiliate entity) must not have been previously suspended or removed from the Services or any other service or product offered by Circle France or its affiliate entities.

items.clause:
8. Closing your Circle Mint Account
8.1. You may close your Circle Mint Account at any time by contacting Circle Support. Where you are required to provide advance notice of closure of your Circle Mint Account, this notice period will not exceed 1 month. There is no specific fee in connection with your closing of your Circle Mint Account.
8.2. You may not terminate your Circle Mint Account if Circle France believes, in its sole discretion, that such closure is being performed in an effort to evade a court order or legal or regulatory investigation or to avoid paying any amounts otherwise due to Circle France.
8.3. If your Circle Mint Account holds a balance at the time of its closure, we will ask you to withdraw your Account Balance within the first year following closure, during which time your Circle Mint Account will be accessible only for the purpose of withdrawing the remaining balance free of charge. After the closure of your Circle Mint Account occurs, you will not be able to access your Circle Mint Account for any other purpose. All withdrawals of Circle Coins will be subject to the provisions applicable to Circle Coins Transfer as set out in clause 10.4.
8.4. You may withdraw any remaining Circle Coins from your Circle Mint Account following closure by contacting Circle Support and requesting that the Account Balance be sent to you in a manner that is reasonably acceptable for us. As set out in clause 8.3. withdrawal of funds during the first year post-closure will be free of charge. However, we reserve the right to charge a recurring annual inactivity fee for those Circle Mint Accounts with residual balances after the first anniversary of closure of the Circle Mint Account onwards. The annual inactivity fee currently in force and that will be applied will be specified in the "Fees" section of our Website and may change from time to time.
8.5. If you want to access your transaction history after the closure of your Circle Mint Account, you will need to contact Circle Support and request the information, you may do so for a period of six years from the date of closure of your Circle Mint Account but we suggest that you redeem your remaining Circle Coins as soon as possible as they will not earn any interest while in your Circle Mint Account. Your obligations with regards to keeping your Circle Mint Account safe as set forth in section 7 (Keeping Your Circle Mint Account Safe) shall continue to apply.
8.6. We reserve the right to carry out any necessary ML, TF, fraud or other illegal activity checks before authorising any withdrawal of your Account Balance, including in relation to returning any funds to you after you have closed your Circle Mint Account.
8.7. We encourage you to redeem or transfer any Circle Coins out of your Circle Mint Account prior to issuing a request to terminate your Circle Mint Account. We may be unable to terminate your Circle Mint Account at your request if you maintain an Account Balance. We reserve the right to restrict or refuse to permit redemptions or transfers from your Circle Mint Account if:
8.7.1. your Circle Mint Account has otherwise been suspended or unilaterally terminated by Circle France in accordance with these Terms of Use; or
8.7.2. to do so would be prohibited by law or a court order or we have determined that any of your Circle Mint Account balance was obtained fraudulently.
8.8. Upon closure or suspension of your Circle Mint Account, you authorise Circle France to cancel or suspend pending transactions.
8.9. In the event that you or Circle France terminates these Terms of Use or you lose access to your Circle Mint Account, you remain liable for all activity conducted on or with your Circle Mint Account while it was active and for all amounts due hereunder.

items.clause:
9. About Circle Coins
9.1. Circle Coins means “EURC” or “USDC”. Please refer to the EURC and USDC White Papers for further information. The applicable White Paper sets out the risks relating to Circle France and to the relevant Circle Coin.
9.2. EURC is an e-money token issued by Circle France that operates primarily on the Ethereum blockchain. EURC is designed, held out and used as an electronic surrogate for coins and banknotes (specifically Euro), a specific character of e-money. Additionally, EURC meets all of the conditions of the definition of e-money under French and European Union laws, and notably MiCA regulation. As such, EURC is e-money for the purposes of the Services and these Terms of Use.
9.3. USDC is an e-money token issued by Circle France that operates primarily on the Ethereum blockchain. USDC is designed, held out and used as an electronic surrogate for coins and banknotes (specifically USD), a specific character of e-money. Additionally, USDC meets all of the conditions of the definition of e-money under French and European Union laws, and notably MiCA regulation. As such, USDC is e-money for the purposes of the Services and these Terms of Use.
9.4. All Circle Coins are fully backed by an equivalent amount of euro-denominated or USD-denominated assets held by Circle France with European Union-based regulated financial institutions in segregated accounts separate from Circle France’s corporate funds, on behalf of, and for the benefit of, Users (the “Segregated Accounts”). This means that for every Circle France Coin issued by Circle France and remaining in circulation, Circle France will hold on behalf of Users either one euro or an equivalent amount of euro-denominated assets or one dollar or an equivalent amount of USD-denominated assets in its Segregated Accounts (the "Reserves").
9.5. Circle Coins are not designed to create returns for holders, increase in value, or otherwise accrue financial benefit to the Circle Coins holder. You will not earn any interest by virtue of your holding Circle Coins in your Circle Mint Account. Note that from time to time, Circle France or its affiliates may offer yield generating Services, but any such Services shall be subject to additional terms and conditions that you would have to separately agree to.
